findings.title: Comparator participant reconciliation omits EMPEROR-Reduced

evidence.quote: DAPA‐HF ( n = 4744) EMPEROR‐Preserved ( n = 5988) EMPEROR‐Reduced ( n = 3730) SOLOIST‐WHF ( n = 1222)

In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 3730 patients with class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to recommended therapy.

findings.why_wrong: Both DAPA-HF and EMPEROR-Reduced contribute selected efficacy estimates, but participant_reconciliation silently skips the latter because its selected effect row lacks participant-count fields. Their combined population is 8474, making the difference from 9199 equal to 725, not 4455. Calling the partial sum the review's population is incorrect.
findings.served_effect: Overstates the comparator population excess by 3730 participants and supplies incorrect numerical evidence for the parity assessment.
findings.proposed_fixture: Use the two current selected efficacy rows plus their held abstracts as input. Assert that participant reconciliation includes both trial identities, returns ours_n=8474 and excess=725; if any denominator remains unresolved, require an incomplete result instead of a partial total. The current function reproduces ours_n=4744.

findings.title: Primary endpoint definition attached to DAPA-HF's selected secondary endpoint

claim.quote: "endpoint_definition": "; DISCLOSED (composite-component difference, found by the cross-family AGY/Gemini audit of the not-yet-audited topics): DAPA-HF (31535829) defines its primary as worsening heart failure — HF HOSPITALISATION or an URGENT HF VISIT requiring IV therapy — or cardiovascular death, whereas EMPEROR-Reduced (32865377) and our outcome label count CV death or HF hospitalisation only. The urgent-visit component is a minor broadening in DAPA-HF; disclosed, still poolable."

evidence.quote:
"type": "SECONDARY",
        "title": "Subjects Included in the Composite Endpoint of CV Death or Hospitalization Due to Heart Failure."
The primary outcome was a composite of worsening heart failure (hospitalization or an urgent visit resulting in intravenous therapy for heart failure) or cardiovascular death.

findings.why_wrong: The selected DAPA-HF result is the registry secondary composite excluding urgent visits. Its endpoint_definition and compatibility metadata instead inherit an audit describing the broader primary composite. The audit statement is accurate about the primary endpoint but is linked to the wrong selected result.
findings.served_effect: Misdescribes the selected estimate as having an urgent-visit component and introduces a nonexistent endpoint difference into compatibility metadata.
findings.proposed_fixture: Use the held DAPA-HF secondary registry outcome and the current definition-audit resolution. Run endpoint-dimension derivation for the selected secondary result. Assert that endpoint_definition follows the selected registry outcome and excludes urgent visits; retain the primary-endpoint audit only as separately scoped context.

findings.title: Comparator trial count declared unstated despite held trial listings

claim.quote: "theirs_k": "not stated in the comparator abstract/full text"

evidence.quote: After removal of duplicate records as well as title/abstract and full‐text screening, four met eligibility criteria
Two trials included only patients with a reduced LVEF, one trial included only patients with a preserved LVEF, and one trial included both.

findings.why_wrong: The held full text explicitly supplies the overall count of four and describes the population distribution relevant to the selected subgroup. Failure to extract a scoped count does not establish that the comparator never states a count.
findings.served_effect: Presents an extraction limitation as source absence and obscures available trial-set evidence.
findings.proposed_fixture: Feed the quoted full-text sentences into comparator count extraction. Assert that overall k=4 is retained with its scope and that subgroup uncertainty, if unresolved, is labelled unextracted rather than 'not stated in the comparator abstract/full text'.

findings.title: Volume-depletion sentence used as ketoacidosis reporting evidence

claim.quote:
"harm_source_reported": true,
          "harm_source_span": "The frequency of adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups.",
          "harm_source_signal": "term_signal"

evidence.quote: The frequency of adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups.

findings.why_wrong: This field sequence occurs in DAPA-HF's diabetic-ketoacidosis row. The cited sentence concerns three other adverse outcomes and does not report ketoacidosis. The generic 'adverse events' keyword causes reporting_signal to attach it to the ketoacidosis outcome; this behavior was reproduced in memory.
findings.served_effect: Counts DAPA-HF as reporting ketoacidosis using an unrelated abstract sentence and gives its outcome-specific refusal an incorrect source link.
findings.proposed_fixture: Pass the exact held adverse-event sentence and the configured diabetic-ketoacidosis specification to reporting_signal. Assert that it yields no ketoacidosis reporting signal; the volume-depletion specification should still match. Require a ketoacidosis-specific held span for a positive ketoacidosis source link.
